stepAge.title: Age Settings
stepAge.retireAge: At what age do you plan to retire?
stepAge.whyAskContent: Knowing your age and expected retirement time allows us to calculate your "accumulation period" — how much time you have to prepare for retirement. Time is compound interest's most powerful ally.
stepAge.theoryContent: The Time Value of Money is a foundational concept in financial planning. The earlier you start, the less you need to invest each month, because time lets compound interest work for you.

validation.retireRequired: Please enter your expected retirement age
validation.retireRange: Retirement age must be between 30 and 100
validation.retireAfterCurrent: Retirement age must be greater than current age

stepExpense.title: Ideal Retirement Expenses
stepExpense.monthlyExpense: What is your ideal monthly expense after retirement?
stepExpense.description: Imagine you've already retired — no student loans or mortgage payments. Purely for food, clothing, housing, transportation, and entertainment, how much per month would make you comfortable?
stepExpense.whyAskContent: The core of retirement planning is understanding "how much money you need to live comfortably." It's not about having as much as possible — it's about finding the number that gives you peace of mind.
stepExpense.theoryContent: The "Replacement Ratio" is a key concept in retirement planning. It's generally recommended that post-retirement spending be about 70-80% of pre-retirement income, but a more precise approach is to directly estimate the cost of your desired lifestyle.

validation.required: Please enter your ideal monthly expense
validation.min: Monthly expense should be at least NT$ 5,000
validation.max: Please enter a reasonable amount (under NT$ 1,000,000)

stepInflation.title: Inflation & Retirement Target
stepInflation.inflationDescription: Inflation erodes purchasing power over time. Today's NT$ 40,000 might only buy half as much in 30 years. We use the inflation rate to estimate how much you'll actually need at retirement.
stepInflation.futureExpense: Estimated annual expense at retirement: NT$ {amount}
stepInflation.whyAskContent: If you ignore inflation, your retirement savings may not be enough. Inflation is like a silent thief, stealing a bit of your purchasing power every year. We must factor this in.
stepInflation.theoryContent: The 4% Rule originated from the 1998 Trinity Study. It found that if you withdraw no more than 4% of your retirement fund each year (equivalent to saving 25 years' worth of expenses), your money has a greater than 95% chance of lasting 30+ years — and may even continue to grow. This rule assumes a balanced portfolio of stocks and bonds.
stepInflation.fourPercentExplain: Future annual expense × 25 = Retirement target. This means withdrawing only 4% of total assets per year. Based on historical data, there's over a 95% probability the funds will last 30+ years.
